notes: Check batch (2026-10-29-check): four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. Every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, skills_listed 209, head 6d3eb7f with uncommitted: true and skill_hash ca223baf..., so all runs were shown the current text, including this round's uncommitted rewordings.

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix. Of these, git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes only Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call; the six ecto-phoenix.md rules and the directive-order rule are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, graded against the current text. The sentences that decide it: "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name, a short literal, or a trailing keyword list: a map or struct that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements." and "A list, map or keyword literal of more than six elements goes one element per line wherever it stands, a module attribute included; ... A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." 0 of 4 violated. haiku-1 (109-116) and sonnet-2 (150-157) build a multi-line map under a name, one field per line, before the call. haiku-2 line 109 (4 fields, 97 characters) and sonnet-1 line 154 (2 fields) bind a map that fits its line on one line, which the last sentence allows; the case check's one-field-per-line clause applies only to a map that would span several lines. The only trailing keyword lists in calls whose result is not bound are short one-liners (sonnet-1 lines 116-117, the render/3 calls). No file has a literal of more than six elements. haiku-2's multi-line fn passed to Multi.insert/3 (lines 98-100) is not a map, struct or keyword argument, and that pipeline's result is bound to multi.

Keep migrations to schema changes: haiku-1 is violated, line 131: execute "UPDATE posts SET published_at = inserted_at" inside the migration's up/0. Its comment (lines 129-130) reads the rule's last clause, do not use application schema modules inside migrations, as permitting a raw-SQL backfill; the 2026-10-23 haiku-1 broke the rule the same way. haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 add only the column and backfill in a separate script. haiku-2's script aliases MyApp.Blog.Post (line 134) and queries it (line 138), which misses the case check but not the rule, per the standard; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 query the "posts" table.

The other six listed rules: 0 of 4 violated. Every run casts only [:title, :body], declares assoc_constraint(:user) and sets user_id on the struct. haiku-1 and haiku-2 publish with Ecto.Multi and Repo.transaction/1 and normalize the four-tuple to {:error, changeset} (both haiku runs used Repo.transact/2 in 2026-10-23); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use Repo.transact/2 with a two-step with. Every listing preloads the author (sonnet-2 by join plus preload), every controller shows via Blog.get_post!/1 over Repo.get!/2, and directives are grouped in order in every module (haiku-1's Post has no @moduledoc; its use is the first line of the module).

Changed rules outside the list, checked for other_violations. The do: rule's new sentences (fn, captures holding a call with arguments, if ..., do: ..., else:, for always a block): no run writes a do: body, an if, a for, or a capture other than haiku-1's &publish_audit_changeset/1 (line 100), so they are not provoked. The pipeline rule's one-line sentence: no pipeline sits on one line in any run. The capture rule's placeholder-order sentence: no run uses &1 or &2. The committed -> clause rule: the only case clauses (haiku-1 and haiku-2 lines 103-104) are 45 and 59 characters, under 70; haiku-2's multi-line fn (lines 98-100) has 66 characters of pattern and body, so its last sentence (a long one becomes a named function) does not apply. Multi.new() |> ... (haiku-1 97-100, haiku-2 95-100) is not counted under Write pipelines, as in 2026-10-22-d and 2026-10-23; the reworded first sentence adds the kind-or-mode case and does not change that reading. No other_violations found: every MyApp.Blog has @moduledoc and @doc on each public function, no single-step pipe, no string error reason. Assumption and reason comments (haiku-1 1-5 and 129-130, haiku-2 1-8, 32, 119-120 and 129-131, sonnet-1 4-6, 21-23 and 85-86, sonnet-2 16-18 and 147-148) say what the code cannot show and are not counted.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all four because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls; the run folder has no formatter configuration that imports Ecto.Query. As in 2026-10-23, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls in locals_without_parens: all four pass, so format_ok is recorded true and nothing goes under Before you finish (haiku-1 line 1 is a 100-character comment, which the formatter leaves alone). Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.
